articles.title: 📸 2nd awards ceremony
articles.excerpt: Photo gallery from the second awards ceremony, celebrating the VINTAGE Mono & Multi categories as well as the Class40 podium finishers. The ceremony took place on the main stage of the MACTe in Pointe-à-Pitre.

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF November 20
articles.excerpt: Ce vendredi 20 novembre, les arrivées se poursuivent à Pointe-à-Pitre. Gilles Lamiré a terminé sixième des Vintage Multi après avoir réparé en mer un flotteur cassé. Dans la même catégorie, la bonification de Romain Pilliard, attendu dimanche matin, pourrait encore modifier l’ordre du podium.

articles.title: 📸 Photos from the edge
articles.excerpt: Les arrivées s’enchaînent en Guadeloupe, mais l’aventure continue pour les skippers encore en mer ! Les derniers milles réservent toujours de belles images, des sourires et quelques surprises. Découvrez leurs dernières photos envoyées depuis l’Atlantique !

articles.title: The return of the local boy
articles.excerpt: The skipper of Drépavoile (Class40) arrived in the early morning in the bay of Pointe-à-Pitre. In a joyful and festive atmosphere, the first Guadeloupean in this 2026 edition savored his arrival. 37th four years ago, 24th this year, he is further establishing himself as the best skipper in the archipelago.

articles.title: And meanwhile, on the water...
articles.excerpt: While the MACTe dock became as congested as a major holiday traffic jam, on the water, the last competitors continued their journey towards the archipelago. Some were eager to finish, others, so thrilled to be discovering the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe, weren't really keen to see Tête à l'Anglais just yet.

articles.title: The Rum Solidarity
articles.excerpt: This is the epilogue to the most beautiful story of this Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe. After a perilous rescue, a forced cohabitation of ten days in the middle of a solo race and a magnificent eighth place at the finish, the improvised duo of Jules Bonnier (Plastic Odyssey) and Benoît Sineau (Ekinox Rhétorès) transformed a maritime misfortune into a moving lesson in solidarity.

articles.title: Tanguy Caradec: "If my father is watching us from up there, I hope he's proud too."
articles.excerpt: The Vintage Mono podium is now set! After Kieran Le Borgne (Armor-Lux – Le Finistère Assurance, 1st) and Sidney Gavignet (Le Cigare Rouge, 2nd), it's Tanguy Caradec's (Eurvad, 3rd) turn to finish. Arriving at 9:37 PM (local time) and 2:37 AM (Paris time), he completed the race in 16 days, 13 hours, and 35 minutes. Forty years after the tragic death of his father, Loïc Caradec, in 1986, Tanguy fulfilled "his lifelong dream" by controlling the race from start to finish.

articles.title: Sidney Gavignet: "The boat took care of me"
articles.excerpt: FLASH FINISH. The skipper of Le Cigare Rouge finished 2nd in the Vintage Mono class after crossing the finish line this Tuesday at 6:31 pm (local time), 11:31 pm (Paris time). After 16 days, 10 hours, and 29 minutes of racing, Sidney Gavignet took 2nd place in the Vintage Mono class, 20 hours and 52 minutes behind the winner, Kieran Le Borgne (Armor-Lux – Le Finistère Assurance).

articles.title: Florian Gueguen: "This race will remain unforgettable"
articles.excerpt: The intense heat that beat down on the pontoon of honor early Tuesday afternoon did nothing to dampen the festive spirit. Family and friends of Florian Gueguen (Graine de Courage) were there with signs, horns, face paint, and the intention of adding to the excitement. It was amidst this celebratory hubbub that the skipper, who crossed the finish line in 3rd place in the Vintage Multi class, moored his boat.

articles.title: Florian Gueguen crosses the finish line in 3rd position in Vintage Multi!
articles.excerpt: FLASH FINISH. After Damien Seguin (Arkéa Handicap International, winner) and Éric Péron (French Touch - Oceania Hotels, 2nd), Florian Gueguen was the third in his category to cross the finish line in Pointe-à-Pitre this Tuesday at 12:42 PM (local time) and 5:42 PM (Paris time). He completed the race in 16 days, 4 hours, and 40 minutes. However, the final podium will only be known once Romain Pilliard has arrived. The skipper of Use it Again received a time bonus of 6 days and 18 hours...

articles.title: Class40: A wave of new arrivals
articles.excerpt: Throughout Monday night and into Tuesday morning, Class40 skippers took turns at the docks. Pep Costa (VSF Sports, 8th), Luca Rosetti (Macaferri Futura, 9th), and William Mathelin Moreaux (Patapain – Les Invincibles, 10th) completed the top 10. Ian Lipinski (Crédit Mutuel, 11th), Milan Kolacek (Inland Roots Ocean Soul, 12th), Sophie Faguet (Défi Solidaire – with Ellye and L'Arche, 13th), and Mikael Mergui (Hirsch – Centrakor, 14th) also finished.

articles.title: Six winners, and still plenty of trouble!
articles.excerpt: Six categories, six winners. With Kieran Le Borgne's victory in the Vintage Mono class, the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026 has crowned all its winners. But the race is far from over. In Pointe-à-Pitre, boats are arriving one after another, sometimes just minutes apart. Elsewhere, the gaps are closing, time bonuses are complicating the calculations, and some sailors still have a thousand miles to go. In short, the results are almost complete, but the show refuses to end!

articles.title: Kieran Le Borgne: “I feel overwhelmed by emotions”
articles.excerpt: He arrived in the early evening, and a festive atmosphere gradually took over the pontoon. Kieran Le Borgne (Armor Lux - Le Finistère Assurance) had just won the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe and was on cloud nine. Everything was a blur, and his eyes were misty. During the interview, he managed to hold back his tears, sharing them with his loved ones a few minutes later. His parents, his partner, and his friends surprised him by being there to make the night even more special....

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF November 17
articles.excerpt: Ce mardi 17 novembre, la victoire de Kieran Le Borgne en catégorie Vintage Mono complète le palmarès de la Route du Rhum 2026. Mais la course se poursuit sur un Atlantique où le vent reste très hétérogène. Autour de la Guadeloupe, les grains et les dévents peuvent encore redistribuer les places.
